source.title: Stabilizing Quantization-Aware Training by Implicit-Regularization on Hessian Matrix

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the proposed relationship between flat loss landscapes and generalization to motivate a quantization-aware training method, then reports that method's results. It does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports FPQ accuracy comparisons and Hessian-trace comparisons. These concern quantization-aware training and do not measure the natural-label versus random-label generalization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or example-removal effects in the versions. Hessian trace is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization relationship to motivate feature-perturbed quantization and evaluates its method. It does not test V1–V8. Its Hessian trace is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness, and it reports neither train–test gaps nor comparisons of generalization-measure rankings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that stochastic feature perturbations with standardized feature distillation implicitly regularize the Hessian, smooth the loss landscape, improve stability, and improve QAT performance. Their broad superiority language needs qualification: Table 5 includes settings where FPQ trails LSQ or other baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Uses feature perturbations and channel-wise standardized feature distillation in quantization-aware training; it does not use the original studies' interventions or measures for the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that FPQ probability p affects CIFAR-10 W2A4 validation accuracy, with an optimal range of 0.1 to 0.5; these values are method-selection results and are not extracted as claim rows.

fits_no_version.finding: FPQ has lower reported Hessian-trace trajectories than LSQ for ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2 on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature perturbations combined with feature distillation can reduce Hessian trace during quantization-aware training.

fits_no_version.finding: For CIFAR-10 W4A4 quantization, FPQ exceeds LSQ+SAM accuracy by 0.41 percentage points on ResNet-18 and 0.81 points on MobileNetV2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FPQ can outperform LSQ+SAM in quantized-model classification accuracy.

record.problems: The reported Hessian-trace comparisons are figure-only, without numerical values or uncertainty. The paper does not report a training-versus-test error gap for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other QAT accuracy comparisons in Tables 2, 4, and 5 are method-performance results and do not measure any listed claim version or the train-test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and dependence on tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical discussion concerns sensitivity to quantization and assumes correlated training and validation losses; it does not establish V7's empirical correlation or comparative ranking. Stochastic feature perturbation is not a dropout comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning recipes.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian-trace trajectories for FPQ and LSQ during training.
rows.note: The text says the proposed method's Hessian trace is significantly lower than LSQ's; no numeric values are stated.
rows.check: Figure 5(a) and Section 4.3 report lower Hessian trace for FPQ than LSQ, but this cannot establish any listed version. This is a method-characterization result; observed describes the trace reduction, not V7.
